```{r setup}
source_cells <- read.csv("data/extracted/long.csv", check.names = FALSE)
runs <- read.csv("data/review/runs.csv", check.names = FALSE)
decisions <- read.csv("data/decisions.csv", check.names = FALSE)
agreement <- read.csv("data/review/reader_agreement.csv", check.names = FALSE)
round1 <- read.csv("data/review/reread_key.csv", check.names = FALSE)
round2 <- read.csv("data/review/reread_key_round2.csv", check.names = FALSE)
author_review <- read.csv("data/review/author_review.csv", check.names = FALSE)
amended <- runs[runs$run_label == "amended", ]
first <- runs[runs$run_label == "first", ]
consolidated <- runs[runs$run_label == "consolidated", ]
qa <- agreement[agreement$sample == "qa", ]
checks <- read.csv("data/review/consolidated_check_results.csv", check.names = FALSE)
automatic <- sum(!grepl("^Author", decisions$evidence))
image_checks <- decisions[grepl("cell without reread", decisions$evidence), ]
pending <- sum(is.na(author_review$author_value))
matches <- function(column) !is.na(author_review[[column]]) &
  author_review$author_value == author_review[[column]]
# Exclusive attribution: retain OCR first, then Claude, then Codex, then manual.
kept_ocr <- matches("ocr_value")
kept_claude <- !kept_ocr & matches("claude_reading")
kept_codex <- !kept_ocr & !kept_claude & matches("codex_reading")
manual <- !kept_ocr & !kept_claude & !kept_codex
funnel <- data.frame(
  Stage = c("Printed cattle cells", "Alarm candidates (amended run)",
            "Reread round 1", "Reread round 2", "Automatic decisions",
            "Cells sent to author review", "Pending after author review"),
  Cells = c(nrow(source_cells), amended$n_candidates, nrow(round1),
            nrow(round2), automatic, nrow(author_review), pending)
)
```

## Source and pipeline

The source is the cattle table on printed pages 161–164 (PDF pages 162–165) of
the 1950 Mexican agricultural census. The [README](README.md) documents the
source inventory, checks, and decision files. The pipeline preserves each OCR
literal and applies recorded decisions. Before author review, unresolved cells
were sent to a stable review file; that file now retains all reviewed cells,
with each decision beside its original reading.

## Method

At gate A, each cell is mapped by its printed position, which determines its
geography and holding category; OCR row order does not define the table. At gate
B, approved OCR rules remove spaces, read `O`, `L`, `G`, `I`, `]`, and `J` as
digits, and drop stray hyphens, periods, and commas. These rules make a value
readable, not right. The original literal remains available beside every
normalized value.

The arithmetic checks apply separately to each printed measure $m$, holding
$h$, and entity $g$. For cattle heads and pesos, the within-holding identity is
$S_{g,h,m} = F_{g,h,m} + C_{g,h,m}$, where $S$, $F$, and $C$ denote *suma*,
*fino*, and *corriente*. The holding identity is
$X_{g,\text{total},m} = \sum_{h \neq \text{total}} X_{g,h,m}$. Geographic
aggregation checks states against regions and regions against the nation:
$X_{r,h,m} = \sum_{g \in r} X_{g,h,m}$, followed by the equivalent sum of
regions to the national value, $X_{\text{national},h,m} = \sum_r X_{r,h,m}$.
An identity with any required component missing is not evaluated; a missing
value is never treated as zero.

Gate C sends unread cells and cells whose row and column checks both fail to a
review queue, alongside a random no-alarm sample for quality assurance.
Claude and Codex read each crop blind to the OCR value and to each other's
reading; the same two-reader blind protocol is repeated in round two on
companion cells from identities that still fail. At gate D, R2 accepts matching readings only when both identities pass;
R3 accepts the sole reading that passes both when readers disagree. R4
reconstructs a unique component as $\hat{x} = T - \sum_{j \neq x} x_j$ and
accepts it only when the row and column identities both hold. A printed-source
discrepancy is recorded when OCR and both readers agree, every failing identity
has $|T - \sum_j x_j|/T < 0.01$, and the published value is retained; a gap of
at least one percent goes to author review. Otherwise, R5 sends unresolved
cases to the author. The two closure rules are that a
companion enters the active queue only if neither reader matches the OCR, and
that matching queued readings count jointly as provisional values under R2.
Arithmetic, not the reader, is the arbiter.

## Review funnel

The first OCR policy left `r first$n_pendiente` unread cells,
`r first$n_alarms` alarms and `r first$n_candidates` candidate cells.
The amended policy left `r amended$n_pendiente` unread cells and
`r amended$n_alarms` alarms: making more values readable also made
more identities evaluable. These two stages are the `first` and `amended` rows
preserved in `data/review/runs.csv`.

The amended checks identified `r amended$n_candidates` candidate cells from
`r nrow(source_cells)` printed cells. The review then covered:

```{r}
knitr::kable(funnel, col.names = c("Stage", "Cells"), caption = "Review funnel")
```

These stages overlap and refer to different selections; their counts must not
be added. The first round includes the 30 no-alarm QA cells; the second covers
96 companion cells. Together they comprise 188 unique crops, each read by both
agents.

The `r automatic` automatic decisions, `r nrow(author_review)` author decisions
on the review queue and `r nrow(image_checks)` author corrections of cells outside
it make `r nrow(decisions)` recorded decisions, preserving each original OCR value.
After consolidation, `r sum(checks$status == "fail")` of `r nrow(checks)`
identities fail and `r pending` cells remain pending.
The earlier closure, preserved in commit `4b2e014`, had 39 decisions and
26 pending cells (`data/decisions.csv` and the `consolidated` row of
`data/review/runs.csv` at that commit). Sending those 26 cells to the author
remains a stage of the process after their decisions have been integrated.

## Claude and Codex

The two readers agreed on `r sum(agreement$readers_agree == "yes")` of
`r nrow(agreement)` crops. The no-alarm QA sample contains `r nrow(qa)` cells:
Claude differed from OCR in `r sum(qa$claude_matches_ocr == "no")`, and Codex in
`r sum(qa$codex_matches_ocr == "no")`. Reader agreement alone does not establish
that a value matches the printed page; the identities provide an independent
check.

## State totals

The maps use state totals from the consolidated table. Boundaries are the 2025
INEGI state geometries; Baja California Sur and Quintana Roo were territories
in 1950, and Distrito Federal is shown as Mexico City. Grey is the map's
missing-value colour. All 32 state totals needed for these maps are available;
there are no pending cells after author review. The retained image legend
"Grey: pending author review" describes the earlier conditional display rule,
not the current review status.

```{r maps, out.width="100%", fig.show="hold", fig.cap="State cattle heads; cattle value per head; and the share of heads classified as fino."}
knitr::include_graphics(c("data/consolidated/map_heads.png",
                          "data/consolidated/map_value_per_head.png",
                          "data/consolidated/map_fine_share.png"))
```

Value per head is total cattle value divided by total cattle heads. Fine share
is *fino* cattle heads divided by total cattle heads.

## Author review

The author checked `r nrow(author_review)` cells on the printed page and closed
the review queue: `r sum(kept_ocr)` retain the OCR value,
`r sum(kept_claude)` adopt Claude's reading, `r sum(kept_codex)` adopt Codex's
reading, and `r sum(manual)` use a manual value. These counts are exclusive:
an unchanged OCR value counts as retained even if a reader agrees, and a changed
value shared by both readers counts with Claude. The author first
recorded Campeche 162:52:3 as a printed-source discrepancy and kept 11 386; on
re-checking the page on 14 October the author read 44 386, the value the four
identities implied, and corrected the decision (D024): one row of
`data/review/author_review_amendments.csv` and a rerun. The stable queue
keeps all decisions alongside the readings, with `r pending` pending cells.

For R087 (Sinaloa, 163:38:4), four identities imply 2 once the San Luis Potosí
OCR error (corrected below) is accounted for in the national identity;
the row, Sinaloa total and Pacífico Norte identities imply 2 directly.
For Yucatán 163:15:4 (R019), OCR, both readers and the author's first reading
were 3192, but the arithmetic implies `r author_review$author_value[author_review$reread_id == "R019"]`
and a second look at the page confirms it.

After D024, 16 identities still failed. They pointed to four locations and five
cells that had never been reread, because their alarms appeared only once the
queue was closed: Tabasco 163:3:3 and 163:3:5, Baja California Sur 163:29:5 and
San Luis Potosí 162:33:4 and 162:35:4. They looked like printed discrepancies.
On 15 October the author checked the five cells against the page image: the page
prints the value the identities imply in every case, so all five were OCR
errors, not discrepancies in the source.

```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Cell = image_checks$cell, OCR = image_checks$ocr_literal,
                        Page = format(image_checks$decided_value, big.mark = " "),
                        Decision = image_checks$decision_id),
             caption = "Cells corrected against the page image (15 October 2026)")
```

The OCR lost the thousands digit in Tabasco and Baja California Sur and read
4 as 1 and 6 as 0 in San Luis Potosí. Each correction is one row of
`data/review/author_review_amendments.csv` under the signed rule
`decision_cell_amendment` (`data/check_policy.csv`): the author may correct a
cell that was never reread by checking it against the image. No value was set
to force an identity: the page was read, and the identities confirmed the reading.
